VERDICT: DISAGREE. Three blocking items.

B1. THE PROOF RECORD MAKES A COVERAGE CLAIM THAT A MUTATION PROBE FALSIFIES. This is the finding I consider decisive, and it is in none of the three prior records.
proof/44.json acceptance_criteria[6] is recorded "met": true and reads:
    "NOTICE diagnostics in _api() AND emit_find_prs() go to sys.stderr; ... (independent review finding #1, fixed; PINNED BY test_emit_find_prs_unresolved_prints_empty_prs_and_does_not_fail asserting the exact stdout line structure and that NOTICE text lands on stderr)"
The same claim is repeated in that test's own docstring: "This also pins the fix for a real defect: `_api` AND `emit_find_prs` used to print their `NOTICE: ...` diagnostics to stdout".
The _api() half is not pinned by anything. PROBE, reverting ONLY _api()'s two NOTICE prints from stderr back to stdout and leaving emit_find_prs() untouched:
    $ python -m pytest tests/ -q
    535 passed in 20.26s
Zero failures across the entire suite. The reason is structural and visible in the named test itself: it does `monkeypatch.setattr(auto_queue, "resolve_pr_numbers", lambda event, event_name: None)`, so _api() is never called during that test, and the assertions `stdout_lines == ["prs="]` / `"NOTICE" not in captured.out` can only ever observe emit_find_prs()'s own NOTICE.
The consequence is not hypothetical. With _api() reverted I drove the real emit_find_prs() with _run stubbed to a failing gh invocation and captured what the step would append to $GITHUB_OUTPUT:
    |NOTICE: gh api repos/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-BuildCraft/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=100 exited 1: boom: gh not authenticated
    |prs=
PRECISION, because the PR's own comment overstates this in one direction: that particular line DOES contain '=' (inside 'base=main'), so the Actions runner would not reject it outright -- it would parse it as an output variable named 'NOTICE: gh api repos/.../pulls?state'. The other _api() NOTICE ("gh api {path} returned non-JSON") contains no '=' and would fail the step. So both corruption modes exist and neither is caught by a test.
The shipped code is CORRECT -- I want to be exact about that, because a reviewer who blurs "the code is wrong" with "the claim about the code is wrong" is worse than useless. What is wrong is a Proof of Completion recording "met": true for a guard that does not exist, in a repository whose stated purpose for these records is that a check which is not running must never look like a check that is passing. Fix is roughly five lines: one test that lets _api() actually execute (stub _run, assert the NOTICE lands on stderr and stdout holds only `prs=`), or narrow criterion 7 and the docstring to claim only emit_find_prs().

B2. THE STATED REASON FOR THE Handoff TRIGGER IS FALSE AS MEASURED. The PR body (fix item 1), auto-queue.yml's TRIGGERS comment, and the new test's own assertion message all assert:
    "Firing only on CI finishing would read Handoff's check while still pending, `_all_required_checks_green` returns NOT READY, and nothing retries"
_all_required_checks_green only ever examines the contexts _required_contexts() returns, and that function reads the live branch ruleset. I read it:
    $ gh api repos/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-BuildCraft/rules/branches/main --jq '.[]|select(.type=="required_status_checks")|.parameters.required_status_checks[].context'
    test (ubuntu-latest, 3.10) / test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12) / test (windows-latest, 3.10) /
    test (windows-latest, 3.12) / test (macos-latest, 3.10) / test (macos-latest, 3.12) /
    lwb-portable (ubuntu-latest) / lwb-portable (windows-latest) / lwb-portable (macos-latest)
Nine contexts, and 'Handoff' is not among them -- nor is any context Handoff produces. A pending Handoff check therefore cannot make _all_required_checks_green return NOT READY; it is not looked at. Furthermore every one of those nine contexts is produced by the CI workflow, whose workflow_run 'completed' event fires only once all its jobs have finished -- so firing on CI alone is already sufficient, and the stall the comment describes cannot occur.
Listening to Handoff as well is harmless belt-and-braces and I am not asking for it to be removed. I am asking for the justification to be corrected, in all three places, because it is a measured-sounding claim that is not true, and this repository has an explicit history of scoped claims stated as though general. No code change is required for this one.

N2. THE TRIGGER NAMES ARE NOT CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE REAL WORKFLOWS. The test hardcodes "CI" and "Handoff". PROBE: change ci.yml's `name: CI` to `name: Continuous Integration` -> 26 passed, 0 failed. The workflow_run trigger is now dead and the suite is green -- the exact shape of this PR's headline defect (a trigger that never fires, silently), and the same shape as a secret referenced under a name the repository does not have. Assert instead that every entry in workflow_run.workflows equals some tracked workflow's `name:` field. Combined with N1 that is one small test covering both.
N3. A SIBLING FIELD THAT CHANGES THE MEANING IS STILL IGNORED -- record 01TkEV63's N1, unaddressed. `workflow_run: types: [completed]` fires for conclusion 'failure', 'cancelled' and 'skipped' as readily as 'success'; resolve_pr_numbers reads workflow_run["head_sha"] and never ["conclusion"] or ["name"]. Harmless (_all_required_checks_green stops it) but wasteful: a failed CI run drives a full resolve-and-enqueue attempt. One line: `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`.
N4. THIS PR MAKES AUTO-MERGE LIVE FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THE BODY DOES NOT SAY SO. The automatic path has never fired in this repo's history; after this lands, the 15-minute sweep enqueues every open PR against main whose required checks are green. The ruleset's pull_request rule has required_approving_review_count: 0, so no human approval is involved. I am recording this as a consequence to accept deliberately, NOT as a defect -- see the near-miss below, which is the reason I am confident it is safe.
N5. The sweep's `pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=100` is unpaginated. Above 100 open PRs it silently truncates -- "checked and found some" reported as "checked and found all". Far from binding today (5 open PRs); noted so it is not rediscovered.
N6. THE GATE CANNOT PASS UNTIL SOMEONE REMOVES THE STALE RECORDS, AND THIS VERDICT DOES NOT CHANGE THAT EITHER WAY. _review_ok appends an ERROR for any record that is DISAGREE or stale, and check_lanes fails on any error -- it is not "at least N AGREE", it is "N AGREE and nothing invalid". The three records at 108d87d are now BOTH stale and DISAGREE, so reviews/44/ blocks lwb-lanes on its own. Had I voted AGREE, lwb-lanes would still fail. Whoever resolves this must supersede or remove them; that is the author's or owner's call, not mine -- my authorisation is to add a record, and deleting another reviewer's evidence is not something I will do unasked.

NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT AND AM PRINTING, per the honesty rule. Reading the ruleset for B2, I saw that its required contexts are only `test` x6 and `lwb-portable` x3, and I began writing a blocking finding that the new 15-minute sweep could auto-merge shared-path changes without the independent-review gate, because lwb-lanes is not a required context. That would have been a false accusation and a serious one. lwb-lanes is not a separate JOB -- it is a STEP inside the `test` job (ci.yml line 198), with no continue-on-error, and `test` IS required on all six legs. The review gate therefore binds exactly as intended, which is also why N4 above is an observation rather than an objection. I caught it by parsing ci.yml's job/step structure before writing the claim rather than after. The same reading would have wrongly condemned lwb-proof, lwb-commit-identity and lwb-env-leak.
